newsitem.title: CHINA: China smelter Jan-May zinc exports up 135 pct.
newsitem.headline: China smelter Jan-May zinc exports up 135 pct.

text.p: China's Zhuzhou Smelter exported 60,000 tonnes of zinc ingots and zinc products, including alloys, in the first five months of 1997, up 135 percent from the year-ago period, a company official said.
The smelter earned about $80 million through exports of zinc and lead in the first five months, up 22.33 percent compared with the year-ago period, he said.
"It was mainly because of rising international zinc prices," the official said by telephone from Zhuzhou in central Hunan province.
Zhuzhou Smelter's lead exports declined by 25 percent year-on-year in the first five months, he said, without giving export figures. It exported no copper in the period.
The smelter produced 86,000 tonnes of zinc, 2,813 tonnes of copper and 19,487 tonnes of lead in the first five months, the official said.
The company, a subsidiary of the China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp, has the capacity to produce 250,000 tonnes of zinc ingots and high grade zinc slabs each year.
The smelter aims to post a net profit of 45 million yuan ($5.4 million) in 1997, up from about 30 million yuan in 1996, he said.
It plans to produce 200,000 tonnes of zinc, 10,000 tonnes of copper and 70,000-80,000 tonnes of lead in 1997, he said.
But the smelter is facing difficulties meeting copper and lead output targets because of shortfalls of raw materials, he said.
